title: Hallway Emergency Lighting Console
description: The user stands inside a dark spaceship hallway where multiple lanterns serve as emergency lighting sources. A post-processing console lets the user adjust bloom, color grading, vignette, chromatic aberration, and film grain per-lantern and globally, with an undo/redo history and a total energy conservation law that redistributes intensity across all lanterns when one is changed.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with postprocessing via EffectComposer from three/addons. Load space_ship_hallway.glb as the environment and place 4 instances of Lantern.glb at evenly spaced positions along the hallway interior. Set the camera inside the hallway looking down its length with OrbitControls limited to interior panning. Start the scene nearly dark with only faint ambient light (0.05 intensity). Each lantern emits a PointLight whose color and intensity the user controls. Implement a floating HTML overlay console with these controls: (1) a lantern selector (click a lantern in the viewport via raycasting or use numbered buttons to select), (2) per-lantern sliders for bloom threshold (0-1), bloom strength (0-3), and light color via hue rotation (0-360), (3) global sliders for vignette darkness (0-1), chromatic aberration offset (0-0.01), and film grain intensity (0-0.5). Enforce a conservation law: total light energy across all 4 lanterns is fixed at 4.0 units. When the user increases one lantern's intensity, proportionally decrease the others so the sum stays at 4.0. Display the current energy distribution as a bar chart overlay. The bloom pass must react to per-lantern bloom settings by using separate UnrealBloomPass layers or by dynamically adjusting bloom parameters when the selected lantern is dominant in the view. Implement a full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) that records every slider change and lantern selection as a state snapshot, supporting at least 20 levels. Show undo/redo step count in the UI. Add a reset button that animates all values back to defaults over 1 second. The interaction requires: select lantern (1), adjust bloom threshold (2), adjust bloom strength (3), adjust hue (4), observe energy redistribution (5), select second lantern (6), repeat adjustments (7-9), tweak global vignette (10), tweak chromatic aberration (11), undo several steps (12), redo (13). Render at window resolution with antialiasing enabled.
